kb.t: Demotic Magical Papyrus of London and Leiden
kb.th: The Demotic papyrus treats divination as a rite that brings a god into a lamp flame, where a boy medium can see him, hear him and receive true answers.
h: A lamp divination summons a great god together with Boel into the flame ([p. 131](/book/6953aeab77f38f6761bd843f?page=131)).
A boy medium sees and hears the god in the flame and gives true answers to the questions put ([p. 131](/book/6953aeab77f38f6761bd843f?page=131)).

Origen, Against Celsus (Contra Celsum)||.a: Origen argues that if magic (mageia) and sorcery (goeteia), carried out by wicked demons through incantations, exist, then divine power among men must exist too. Practitioners should be examined by life, character and the consequences of their powers. He says all demons have fallen from the good, and that people call them for love spells, hatred spells and hindering actions. Worship of them is alien to those who worship the God over all. A character busy with demon names, herbs, stones and engravings will be abandoned by God to those demons, who are fixed to blood, fat and melodies and may turn on their own clients.

q.t: Who is it that serves demons through certain incantations and trickery and does such things, and who is it that, having become in a place pure and holy according to his own soul and spirit—and I think also his body—to God, and having received some divine spirit, does such things for the benefit of men and the encouragement to believe in the true God?

The things concerning demons are also made clear by those who call upon demons for the sake of so-called love spells or hatred spells, or for the hindrance of actions, or for ten thousand other such things.

But the character that busies itself with the names of demons for the sake of bodily health, love of the body, and worldly fortune, and seeks how it might charm the demons with certain incantations, will be abandoned by God as wicked, impious, and demonic rather than human, to the demons chosen by the one who speaks such things.

Books of Jeu (Bruce Codex)|||Hermetic &.a: Jesus promises the disciples the mysteries of the aeons of the archons, with their seals, numbers and manner of invocation needed to reach each place. As the soul rises it gives seals and apologies to the archons, and the receivers and Virgins of Light seal, baptize and anoint it. One sample rite has the speaker say the seal's name zōphrakas once, hold the number 2889 in the hands, and recite apologies telling the archons to withdraw.

q.t: I will give you the mystery mysterion of the twelve aeons aiones of the archons archontes and their seals sphragides and their numbers psephoi and the manner of their invocation epikaleisthai to reach their places topoi.

And the Virgin of Light (-παρθένος) seals (σφραγίζειν) that soul (ψυχή), and the receivers (παραλήμπται) of the Light baptize (βαπτίζειν) that soul (ψυχή) and give it the spiritual unction (χρῖσμα πνευματικόν), and each of the Virgins of Light (-παρθένοι) seals (σφραγίζειν) it with their seals (σφραγῖδες).

This is its name: zōphrakas; speak it only once, place this number (ψῆφος): 2889 in your hands. But (δέ) when you have sealed (σφραγίζειν) yourselves with this seal (σφραγίς) and have spoken its name only once, then say these apologies (ἀπολογία): >Withdraw (ἀναχωρεῖν) bōzēōth ōxai ēxanatha, for we invoke (ἐπικαλεῖσθαι) zōē zōza ēēzēzōz chōzōēx.

Plotinus, Enneads IV.4.40–44 (magic by s.a: Plotinus asks how sorceries work and answers that they work by sympathy, the natural harmony of likes and the opposition of unlikes. He names Nature as the first enchanter, whose potions and charms people then use on one another. The mage can draw things because the mage is inside the One, and incantations, songs, sounds and shapes carry an innate power of transfer.

q.t: Even when no one is plotting, many things are drawn and enchanted by a natural magic. For true magic is the Friendship in the universe, and also the Strife. This is the primary sorcerer and magician.
Through these, the wretched prepare love-potions and erotic charms; for all licentiousness, and the hope of riches and glory, is through them, and especially deception.
Would that sorcerers also used it always! For then they would not desire to perform sorcery, being blocked by this purity from enjoying those things for which they act impiously.

kb.t: Porphyry, On Abstinence (De abstinentia) II
kb.th: Porphyry argues that eating meat draws impure souls and evil-working daimones to a person and keeps them from God, and that such daimones cause public disasters and blame them on the gods.
h: The theologians avoided animal food lest the impure souls of slaughtered beasts and disturbing daemons be drawn to them and keep them from God ([p. 342](/book/698255f34c90c7f65c860b31?page=342)).
Evil-working daimones cause plagues, famines, earthquakes and droughts ([p. 213](/book/6990616cef12272ffdc8d980?page=213)).
These daimones then persuade people that the beneficent gods did it, and steer them to propitiate the daimones instead ([p. 213](/book/6990616cef12272ffdc8d980?page=213)).
an: Porphyry already held that some daimones are evil; Christian writers went further, ruling that none are good, with Augustine renaming all good intermediaries as angels ([p. 406](/book/69af447846e13536d25887fe?page=406)).

Pistis Sophia|||Hermetic & Gnostic.a: The pages describe the soul's passage after death, when fate and the counterfeit spirit (antimimon pneuma) pursue it, bound to it by the seals and bonds of the rulers. The soul speaks the mystery of the breaking of the seals, which loosens those bonds. Receivers of light and virgins of light then seal, baptize and anoint it before it reaches the treasury of light.

q.t: And when the psychē soul says the mystērion mystery of the breaking of the sphragis seals, at that hour the bonds of the sphragis seals which are bound to the antimimon pneuma counterfeit spirit into the psychē soul are broken.

And the paralemptēs receiver of the light baptizes that psychē soul and they give it the chrisma anointing of the pnikon [uncertain term, possibly relating to purification or spiritual breath]. And the parthenos virgin of the light seals it with their sphragis seals.

What also is the design of names that are without signification? and why, of such, are those that are barbaric preferred to our own? For if he who hears them looks to their signification, it is sufficient that the conception remains the same, whatever the words may be that are used.

why, which is much more absurd than this, are threats employed and false terrors, by any casual person, not to a dæmon, or some departed soul, but to the sovereign Sun himself, or to the Moon, or some one of the celestial Gods

those who invoke the divinities for this purpose have about them stones and herbs, bind certain sacred bonds, which they also dissolve, open places that are shut, … Nor are the artificers of efficacious images to be despised. For they observe the motion of the celestial bodies

there are some who suppose that there is a certain obedient genus of dæmons, which is naturally fraudulent, omniform, and various, and which assumes the appearance of Gods and dæmons, and the souls of the deceased

kb.t: Porphyry, Letter to Anebo
kb.th: Porphyry puts sceptical questions to the ritual practitioners: why they use meaningless foreign names, threaten the heavenly gods, and may be deceived by daemons posing as gods.
h: Porphyry asks why invocations use names without meaning, and barbarian ones rather than Greek, when the god invoked speaks no human language ([p. 45](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=45)).
He objects that practitioners aim threats and false terrors at the Sun, the Moon and the celestial gods ([p. 43](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=43)).

He describes invokers who carry stones and herbs, tie and untie 'sacred bonds', open shut places and change people's intentions, and image-makers who time their work by the stars ([p. 41](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=41)).
He reports a view that a shape-shifting, fraudulent kind of daemon impersonates gods and the dead and produces what appears in the rites ([p. 42](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=42)).
tr: Iamblichus' reply defends the practice as theurgy, a union with the gods produced by ritual acts and symbols known only to the gods, not by thinking ([p. 142](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=142)).
an: Iamblichus answers that the barbarous names cannot be translated without losing their power and suit the gods for their concision ([p. 328](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=328)).
Iamblichus reads the threats as showing the rank of a theurgist who commands mundane natures by arcane signatures, not as meant literally ([p. 314](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=314)).

Augustine reports that Porphyry granted theurgy only the purification of the soul's image-receiving part and wavered on whether it should be banned by law ([p. 235](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=235)).

Asclepius (the Latin Hermetic dialogue)|.a: The Hermes of this dialogue says that man is the fashioner of gods and that a human spirit can be drawn into an idol and stay there for long periods. He calls the statues animated and filled with spirit. Demons are named among the agents that give species their forms, and a person who joins himself to the demons approaches them.

q.t: Repeatedly enticed into the idol, the human spirit endures for long times; thus, man is the fashioner of gods, and you should not think the effects are secondary or earthly, O Asclepius.
Statues, O Asclepius, you see, these which you yourself said, statues animated, these are filled with spirit.

For it is impossible for bodies to be given form without the divine will, for species to be shaped without the assistance of demons, or for living creatures [original: "animalia"] to be established and cared for without the involvement of humans.
I am the headless 145 demon with the face upon my feet; I am the strong one who possesses the immortal fire.
To banish anger: > 'Will you dare to raise the mighty spear against Zeus?'
For I am about to behold today with immortal eyes—I, who was born mortal from a mortal womb
Persephone, 2750 three-headed, fire-roamer, cow-eyed, heifer-feeder, all-feeder, Phorbara; Aktiōphi, Ereschigal

kb.t: Greek Magical Papyri (Papyri Graecae Magicae)
kb.th: The papyri are working handbooks of rites for exorcism, love binding, divination and ascent, in which the practitioner speaks as the god and draws on Greek, Egyptian and Mesopotamian powers.
h: In the Headless One rite the practitioner asks the god to deliver a possessed person and then speaks in the god's person: 'I am the headless demon' ([p. 208](/book/6953ae7f77f38f6761bd7e65?page=208)).
The Paris papyrus uses single lines of Homer's Iliad as charms, one of them to banish anger ([p. 110](/book/6953ae7f77f38f6761bd7e65?page=110)).
The so-called Mithras Liturgy asks to be reborn in thought and to behold the immortal beginning ([p. 111](/book/6953ae7f77f38f6761bd7e65?page=111)).

A love-compulsion spell invokes Hekate with Persephone and the Mesopotamian underworld goddess Ereschigal, and another love binding uses two wax figures, one bound and kneeling ([p. 181](/book/6953ae7f77f38f6761bd7e65?page=181)); ([p. 99](/book/6a3f01fe661123baf6fe996d?page=99)).
A Demotic lamp divination summons a great god with Boel into the flame so that a boy medium sees and hears him and gives true answers ([p. 131](/book/6953aeab77f38f6761bd843f?page=131)).
an: Audollent quotes the Paris papyrus's wax-figure love binding alongside the curse tablets ([p. 99](/book/6a3f01fe661123baf6fe996d?page=99)).

q.t: For a conception of the mind does not conjoin theurgists with the Gods; … For the perfect efficacy of ineffable works, which are divinely performed in a way surpassing all intelligence, and the power of inexplicable symbols, which are known only to the Gods, impart theurgic union.

it is requisite to consider these, and all the best dispositions of the soul, and also the purity pertaining to us, as certain concauses; the things which properly excite the divine will being divine synthemata themselves.

though it should be possible to translate them, yet they no longer preserve the same power when translated. Barbarous names, likewise, have much emphasis, great conciseness, and participate of less ambiguity, variety, and multitude.

What also is the design of names that are without signification? and why, of such, are those that are barbaric preferred to our own? For if he who hears them looks to their signification, it is sufficient that the conception remains the same, whatever the words may be that are used.

kb.t: Iamblichus, On the Mysteries (De mysteriis)
kb.th: Replying to Porphyry, Iamblichus holds that theurgy unites the soul with the gods through rites and symbols known only to the gods, with the divine tokens as the true cause and human thought and purity only secondary.
h: Theurgic union with the gods comes from ritual acts performed beyond understanding and from divine symbols, not from thinking ([p. 142](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=142)).
The divine tokens (synthemata) move the divine will, while the practitioner's purity and good dispositions are only contributing causes ([p. 143](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=143)).

Against Porphyry's question about meaningless foreign names, Iamblichus holds that the barbarous sacred names lose their power in translation and suit the gods by their concision ([p. 328](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=328)); ([p. 45](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=45)).
The theurgist's threats show the rank of one who commands mundane natures as if among the gods, and are not meant literally ([p. 314](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=314)).

Natural sympathy is a real but subordinate cause of sacrifice's power, since the leading cause is the demiurgic powers and the gods are not bound to matter ([p. 275](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=275)); ([p. 273](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=273)).
tr: Iamblichus's term is theourgia, a practitioner's word for rites that work union with the gods; in the Greek split it stands on the licit side against goeteia, so English "magic" lumps together what he keeps apart ([p. 142](/book/69d149ce1c2a66dc094b30c3?page=142)).
an: Ficino rendered the work into Latin sense for sense rather than word for word, framed as Abammon's reply to Porphyry's questions on daemons, prophecy, magic and sacrifice, and this paraphrase is the version the Renaissance read ([p. 13](/book/69592b3b7c072c27f686e213?page=13)).
In Ficino's digest the Egyptian threats to break the heavens are redirected from the celestial gods to an unreasoning, divided power in the world ([p. 164](/book/69b51ebccf111105c42a3afa?page=164)).

k.g: chance utterances believed to be divine

q.t: Since he was truly a god, he took Abaris aside and showed him his golden thigh
In place of the divination performed through the sacrifice of animals, he taught foreknowledge through numbers.
almost everyone affirms that on one and the same day, he was both in Metapontum in Italy and in Tauromenium in Sicily
by whom he was purified from the stains of his former life and was taught that from which serious and diligent men must remain pure.

kb.t: Iamblichus, On the Pythagorean Life
kb.th: Iamblichus presents Pythagoras as a god in human form and a wonder-worker, purified by a Chaldean and teaching foreknowledge by numbers in place of divination by sacrifice.
h: Pythagoras privately showed Abaris his golden thigh as proof that he was the god, after Abaris gave him Apollo's arrow ([p. 120](/book/69c88efc6c6f3cc53c85b25e?page=120)).
He taught Abaris to foresee the future through numbers instead of by reading sacrifices ([p. 120](/book/69c88efc6c6f3cc53c85b25e?page=120)).
Pythagoras was in Metapontum and Tauromenium on the same day, and Iamblichus says almost everyone affirms it (p. 21).
In Babylon the Chaldean Zabratus purified Pythagoras from the stains of his former life ([p. 31](/book/695593407bd6d2cd1d61bc02?page=31)).
an: Zimmermann's De miraculis (1734) argues that the disciples invented the miracles to spread Pythagoras's fame, citing Iamblichus's own promise to adorn the wonders and his appeal to almost everyone for the impossible bilocation (p. 386).

Testament of Solomon|||Early Christian &.a: The narrative shows the seal of God working as a means of command. Struck on the chest with it, the demon Ornias is bound and made to answer, and he names Michael as the angel who thwarts him. Solomon then sends a boy with the seal to fetch other demons, such as Ephippas and those guarding the purple pillar in the Red Sea, and they carry loads through the air.

q.t: And you, Solomon, examine him so that he may show you all his plots. And you, with this seal, shall strike every devil and his power, and you shall gather them all—those of the air, and of the earth, and of the sea, and of the underworld—and you shall build the temple of God with these evil demons, and they shall be laborers for the craftsmen.
And the king asked each one of the demons for their name, their work, and by which of the holy angels they are thwarted. And they confessed their work, their name, and the angel who thwarts them.

The boy sealed all the demons with the seal of God and said to them: "Take this pillar and come, so that we may go to King Solomon." Immediately, those demons took the purple pillar upon themselves, carrying it and bringing it through the air.

Eusebius, Preparation for the Gospel (Pr.a: Eusebius quotes Porphyry's report of an oracle in which a god says magic was given by the gods as a dissolution of the things of Fate. Eusebius answers that the god did not dissolve the decrees for his own temple, and that the same author confesses the gods lie. He calls the rites malicious sorcery involving lifeless statues, Isiac shapes and the charaktēres that Hecate is said to love. He says Christians drive away the works of demons with the name of Jesus and pure prayers, while sorcerers work with libations, sacrifices and the invocation of demons.

q.t: Through these words, it is clearly shown that magic was given by the gods as a "dissolution" of the things of Fate, in order to change it in some way. These are Porphyry’s words, not mine!
What possible benefit to the gods could come from such malicious sorcery? Why should anything "beloved of God" be found in the meddling with lifeless statues?
Who does not know how, with the very name of Jesus and the purest prayers, we take pleasure in driving away every work of the demons?

Ge Hong, The Master Who Embraces Simplic.a: Ge Hong describes jin zhou incantation and restriction as methods of Wu and Yue that work through vital breath, and he credits them with averting pestilence, quieting hauntings and subduing tigers and snakes. He cites a Compendium of Immortals that teaches summoning spirits and prosecuting ghosts, and he answers critics who deny that such arts exist. He warns that spirits of wood and stone are malign and can spoil medicines, so secret arts are needed for protection.

q.t: In the regions of Wu and Yue, there are methods of jin zhou incantation and restriction, which possess clearly demonstrated efficacy, and these are largely matters of vital breath. Those who know this can enter into the midst of a great pestilence and share a bed with the sick while remaining uninfected themselves.

Furthermore, in the Compendium of Immortals [original: "神仙集"], there are methods to summon spirits and prosecute ghosts, as well as arts that enable people to see spirits. When worldly people hear of them, they call them empty fabrications.

These creatures are all perverse qi malign energies. They never consider granting blessings to humans; they can only produce calamity, and they delight in testing Daoist masters. One must use secret arts to protect oneself and one's accompanying disciples; even then, such entities may still spoil a person's medicine.

Cyranides (Kyranides)|||Hermetic & Gnost.a: The text sets out recipes in which parts of animals, herbs and engraved stones are carried as phylacteries or amulets. These are said to protect against demons, bewitchment, enemies, sorcery and illness, and to bring friendship, success and favour. Some entries also treat disease as the work of a demon and prescribe stones, seeds and feathers against it.

q.t: The claws of the seal's hands, if carried or kept, cast away all snares and bewitchments [original: fascinationes; the influence of the "evil eye"]. Therefore, it will be no inconvenience to also place a claw of the right hand into the amulet.

Indeed, whoever carries this phylactery phylacterium [a protective charm or amulet, often containing written spells or sacred substances] will receive gifts from God that he did not even hope for; he will be honored everywhere, conquering all in both speech and deed, and being rescued from every danger, demon, sorcery, and all malice.
Its right eye, carried in deer leather, makes the wearer lovable, fortunate, and powerful.

Gan Bao, In Search of the Spirits (Soush.a: Gan Bao records gu-sorcery, in which a man keeps a creature in a ritual vessel and dies when it is killed. He also records diviners who use the Book of Changes together with yansheng techniques of suppression, and exorcists who drive out pestilence demons. In several accounts the diviner's hexagram identifies a haunting or possession, and a rite then removes it.

q.t: In his home, he kept a ritual vessel for the Gu [original: 蠱器 (gǔ qì)]. Within this vessel lived a creature—a snake that had the startling appearance of a toad [original: 蝦蟆 (xiámǎ)].

He was skilled in the divination of the Classic of Changes Yijing an ancient Chinese divination manual and proficient in the arts of sorcery and warding off evil yansheng magical techniques to subdue spirits, curses, or misfortune.
Han You cast hexagrams for her and ordered a cloth sack to be made, instructing them to wait until the daughter's affliction flared up, then stretch the sack open across the window frame.

Augustine, On Christian Doctrine (De doc.a: Augustine groups under superstition the books of the haruspices and augurs, ligatures and remedies that medicine condemns, incantations, marks he calls characteres, and hung or bound objects. He lists trivial omens such as a twitching limb, or a stone, dog or boy passing between friends. He cites the dead Samuel's image before Saul and Paul's expulsion of the demon from the ventriloquist woman, and he rejects the casting of horoscopes by the genethliaci.

q.t: Whatever is instituted by men for the making and worshipping of idols is superstitious, pertaining either to the worship of a creature or any part of a creature as God, or to consultations and pacts of signs that are pleasing and agreed upon with demons. Such are the machinations of the magical arts, which poets are accustomed to mention rather than to teach.

Therefore, all arts of this kind, whether of trivial or harmful superstition, arising from a certain pestilential association of humans and demons—as if established by a covenant of unfaithful and deceitful friendship—are to be utterly rejected and avoided by a Christian.

Mahāmāyūrī, the Great Peacock Spell-Quee.a: The spell is called a great boundary-sealing and great protection that eliminates evil vows, spell-craft, evil karma, kṛtyā, kīlana, spirits such as vetāḍa and piśāca, madness, epilepsy, and fears of kings, thieves, water, fire, weapons and famine. Beings who eat filth and those who use bewitchment or sorcery cannot violate the Peacock Wisdom King. The ritual calls for an altar, a painted image with a peacock before it, a start on the first day of the bright fortnight and never in summer, bathing, clean clothes and incense. A dream of a man coming verifies the mantra, and a woman means the heavenly beings have responded.

q.t: This great boundary-sealing and great protection can eliminate all evil vows. May they break all spell-craft and evil karma. May they eliminate the charms of ghosts and harmful invocations.

All such beings who eat filth cannot violate this Buddha Mother Great Peacock Wisdom King. Also, those who use spells of bewitchment or sorcery, or practice evil arts such as Kritika, Kamana, Kurina, Kirna, Vairuna, Chitta, or Pritishaka, cannot violate it.

Before the image, recite the mantra until you fall into a light sleep; if you dream of a man coming, it means the recitation of the mantra has been verified. If you see a woman coming, it means that the heavenly beings one seeks have shown compassion and response.

For at one moment he warns that this art should be avoided as fallacious and dangerous in its very action, and prohibited by laws. At another moment, however, as if yielding to its praisers, he says it is useful for cleansing a part of the soul

a good man in Chaldea, who was putting forth great effort to purify his soul, found his successes frustrated; for another man, powerful in the same arts but moved by envy, had bound the powers summoned by holy prayers so that they would not grant the requests.

Or perhaps Christians established these laws by which magic arts are punished? On the contrary, these laws exist for no other reason than that there is no doubt these sorceries are ruinous to the human race.

Is it not because of this pestilential and wicked doctrine—by which it is said the fruits of others are transferred to other places—that it was written into the Twelve Tables (that is, the most ancient laws of the Romans, as Cicero records) and a punishment established for anyone who did this?

kb.t: Augustine, City of God VIII–X
kb.th: Augustine refuses the Platonists' line between damnable goetia and praiseworthy theurgy and treats magic of every kind as bound to the deceptive rites of demons.
h: Augustine reports the distinction between goetia and theurgy and rejects it, since both are bound to the rites of demons ([p. 235](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=235)).

From Porphyry's story of an envious Chaldaean who bound the powers a rival had summoned, he concludes that theurgy works for evil as well as good ([p. 236](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=236)); ([p. 235](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=235)).

He argues that if magic were the work of gods, pagan Rome would not punish it, citing the Twelve Tables on charmed crops and Apuleius's trial, where Apuleius denied the art ([p. 201](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=201)).

The Hermetic art of animating statues is a detestable art born of error, and the spirits bound to such images are demons, so all the gods of the nations are demons ([p. 206](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=206)); ([p. 372](/book/69af447846e13536d25887fe?page=372)).

Daemones are never good intermediaries between gods and men, only malign spirits, and good intermediaries should be called angels ([p. 365](/book/69af447846e13536d25887fe?page=365)); ([p. 406](/book/69af447846e13536d25887fe?page=406)).
tr: By making goetia and theurgy one demonic thing, Augustine lets the Latin magia become a single umbrella word, an accuser's label that erases the pagan split ([p. 235](/book/699062f5ef12272ffdc8e9d5?page=235)).
an: Vives, commenting on City of God X.9, quotes the Suda that goeteia, mageia and pharmakeia differ: mageia invokes benevolent daemons for some good, goeteia belongs to rites at tombs, and pharmakeia is a deadly potion ([p. 271](/book/69b2fffee5d6d64d8e197d97?page=271)).
Peucer (1560) reports that the pagans separated mageia from goeteia, then defines mageia himself as an art handed down by the Devil through pacts, erasing the distinction (p. 302).

Theodosian Code IX.16 (On magicians, ast.a: A law of Constantius in 357 forbids consulting a haruspex, a mathematicus or a hariolus, and names Chaldeans and magicians whom the common people call malefici. The title also contains a law of 358 that treats all magicians as enemies of the human race and removes the exemption from torture for those of rank. The Interpretation attached to the 357 law restates it as a ban on consulting an invoker of demons or a diviner out of curiosity about the future.

q.t: Many do not hesitate to use magic arts to disturb the elements [referring to the belief that sorcerers could manipulate the weather or natural forces], to undermine the lives of the innocent, and, by summoning spirits, they dare to manipulate events so that each may destroy their enemies through evil arts.

The soothsayer who approaches a stranger's house shall be burned, as shall he who has summoned him through persuasion or bribes, after the confiscation of their goods, and he shall be deported to an island; for those wishing to serve their own superstition will be able to perform the proper rite publicly.

Eznik of Kołb, Refutation of the Sects||.a: Eznik describes the devil as appearing as a dragon, a nehang or a shahapet, and says corporeal beings cannot change into other forms. He holds that spirit names such as yushkaparik and hambaru come from human opinion about the shapes demons take. He also denies that sorcerers can cast out demons or harm believers.

k.g: a type of forest or mountain spirit

q.t: He makes them believe that there are also nehangs mythical monsters of the rivers and shahapets guardian spirits of the wilderness. After making them believe this, he manifests himself either in the form of a dragon, or of a nehang, or of a shahapet, so that by this means he may lead man astray from his own Creator.
For it is the way of demons to show themselves in various forms, and people assign names according to these forms.
But the demons cannot bridle true believers through tests, nor can sorcerers do so through demonic power.

the ancient priests, when they considered in natural things a certain kinship and sympathy of some for others, and of manifest things for occult powers, and found all things in all things, they founded their sacred science.

Truly all things pray and sing hymns together to the leaders of their order. But some do so in an intellectual way, some in a rational way, others in a natural way, and others indeed in a sensible way.

the ancients applied some of the earthly things to some of the heavenly ones, whence they drew down divine powers into a lower place, on account of a certain similarity. Truly, similarity itself is a sufficient cause for binding individual things to one another.

Not only in plants, however, which have a vestige of life, but also in stones one may see an imitation and a certain participation in the lights from above … the stone which is called the eye of heaven, or the eye of the Sun, has a shape similar to the pupil of the eye

kb.t: Proclus, On the Hieratic Art (De sacrificio et magia)
kb.th: In Ficino's Latin, Proclus grounds the priests' sacred art in the sympathy of all natural things with one another and with hidden powers, so that likeness draws divine power down through chains of stones, plants and animals.
h: The ancient priests founded their sacred science on the kinship and sympathy of natural things, finding all things in all things ([p. 457](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=457)).
The heliotrope turning toward the sun is a prayer, since all things hymn the leaders of their order, each in its own mode ([p. 457](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=457)).
Similarity is enough to bind things together, as heated hemp catches fire from a lamp it does not touch ([p. 458](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=458)).

Angels, daemons, animals, plants and stones form a solar chain, so the lion fears the more solar rooster and lion-faced solar daemons vanish when shown one ([p. 460](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=460)); ([p. 459](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=459)).
The priests mixed many materials because a single thing has some divine property but not enough on its own to call the deity ([p. 461](/book/68fb0dc412055a03a58d3281?page=461)).

Alexander of Tralles, Therapeutica (amul.a: Alexander says that the regular method of healing needs no outside help, and that he gives amulets for patients who refuse medicines. He cites Galen on the power of incantations and describes remedies drawn from animals, engraved stones and rings with written formulas. He explains some of them as acting by antipathy and asks that such secrets be shown only to those who can keep them.

q.t: But since many sick people, especially if they are rich, want neither to take medicines nor to have enemas applied and force us to remove the pain by means of miraculous amulets, I will endeavor to report on this as well, which I have come to know as useful through my own experience and through credible friends.

Some believe that incantations are like the fairy tales of old women, as I myself did for a long time. But with time and through their evident effects, I have come to the conviction that powers dwell within them; for I have come to know their use for scorpion stings and likewise for bones that had become stuck in the throat and were immediately coughed back up as a result of the incantation.

Take an iron ring, make its band octagonal, and write upon the octagon: "Flee, flee, O bile! The skylark has sought you." Write the character depicted below on the head of the ring [A magical character or sigil resembling a stylized 'H' with loops and a crossbar.].

Jewish Aramaic incantation bowls (Nippur.a: The bowl text addresses its demons directly as charmed, sealed, bound and enchanted, and orders them to depart from the house and property of named people. It lists Liliths, Spirits, Demons, Idol-spirits, the Vow, the Curse, the Invocation and evil Magic among the things to be removed. The binding uses seven spells and seven seals, the name Eldedabya Abi Ponan, a conjuration by the great Prince, and quoted verses from Numbers and Zechariah.

q.t: Wholly charmed and sealed and bound and enchanted [are ye], that ye go away and be sealed and depart from the house [and property?] of Farrûch bar Pušbi and Nêwândûch bath Pušbi and Abândûch bath Pušbi, and that there depart from them (2) all evil Liliths and all Demons and Devils and Spells and Idol-spirits, and the Vow and the Curse and the Invocation, and evil Arts and mighty Works and everything hostile.

Chao Yuanfang, Treatise on the Origins o.a: Chao Yuanfang treats ghostly harm as illness arising from the body's condition. When yin and yang are harmonized and the viscera are strong, wind evils and demonic specters cannot harm a person. When blood and qi are deficient, ghosts offend the upright qi. For snakebite, the text names incantation (jinfa prohibition methods) first and medicine second, with realgar and musk as a fallback, and says mountain dwellers should learn the incantation methods.

q.t: When a woman engages in intercourse with ghosts, her viscera and bowels are deficient and her spirit guardian is weak; hence ghostly qi can infect her with disease.

Whenever one is bitten by a snake, first is incantation [Daoist incantation and ritual prohibition techniques ( jinfa prohibition methods )], second is medicine. If neither of these two is available, one can prepare a full dose of realgar and musk in advance. For this reason, those who dwell in the mountains should be made to know the methods of incantation.
These also use blood and victims, and often touch the bodies of the dead. Necromancers are those by whose incantations the dead appear to be resuscitated to divine and to respond to questions.

Through a certain knowledge of the future and of the infernal powers and their invocations, the arts of auspices, auguries, and those things which are called oracles and necromancy were invented. This is wonderful regarding the deceits of the Magi, whose arts of sorcery proceeded so far that they even resisted Moses with similar signs, turning rods into dragons and waters into blood.

kb.t: Isidore of Seville, Etymologies VIII.9 (On the magi)
kb.th: Isidore defines the magi as the people commonly called malefici, who do harm by chant and by demons summoned with blood, and sorts the related arts of enchantment and divination.
h: Magi are those commonly called malefici, who shake the elements, derange minds and kill by the force of a chant without poison ([p. 328](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=328)).
Magi summon demons with blood and victims and touch corpses, and necromancy adds blood to the corpse because demons love blood ([p. 328](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=328)).
Enchanters work their art with words, and divination is either an art or a madness ([p. 329](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=329)).
Following Varro, divination is sorted by the four elements into geomancy, hydromancy, aeromancy and pyromancy ([p. 329](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=329)).
Casting nativities by the twelve signs was permitted until the Gospel, and after Christ no one should read a nativity from the sky ([p. 330](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=330)).
tr: Isidore equates magus with the common word maleficus, so the learned name for the practitioner is defined by the harm done ([p. 328](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=328)).
His praestigium comes from blinding the sight of the eyes and names illusion, not a power over things, so it does not map onto English "magic" ([p. 331](/book/69af2339285bd73604373fd4?page=331)).
an: The Malleus maleficarum takes the name of the malefici from evil-doing or from thinking ill of the faith, and ranks their heresy as the most malicious kind of divination ([p. 60](/book/69bd9c796120d54bd036f318?page=60)).

Qurʾān 2:102 and 113 (Hārūt and Mārūt; t.a: The verse on Solomon says the devils taught people magic, and names Harut and Marut as the two angels at Babylon who sent it down as a trial. Other chapters show Pharaoh's sorcerers casting cords and rods before Moses, and the sorcerers then declare their belief and ask forgiveness for the sorcery they were compelled to practise.

q.t: And they do not teach anyone until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And [yet] they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. And they do not harm anyone through it except by permission of God.

And cast down that which is in thy right hand; it shall swallow up that which they have wrought; for that which they have wrought is but a sorcerer’s deceit, and the sorcerer shall not prosper, whithersoever he cometh.
He said: Cast ye. And when they had cast down, they enchanted the eyes of the people, and struck them with dread, and they produced a mighty enchantment.

Amoghavajra (tr.), Precious Casket Seal.a: In this sutra the Buddha speaks the dharani to Vajrapani, and a seven-treasure stupa then rises from the ground, emitting a great light. The Buddhas of the ten directions promise protection to anyone who places the dharani in a stupa or image. The sutra also says the scroll itself carries great merit and power wherever it is kept.

q.t: If there are good men and good women who install this essential method and place this dharani within a stupa or image, we, the Buddhas of the ten directions, will follow them wherever they are, and at all times, with our divine power and vows, will add our protection and support.
Wherever this scroll is located, it possesses great merit and great power; it can fulfill all auspiciousness.

There shall not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, one who practices kessem divination, a me'onen soothsayer, a menachesh augur, a mechashef sorcerer, 220 a charmer, one who consults a ghost or a spirit, or a doresh el hametim one who inquires of the dead; for all who do these things are an abomination to the Lord your God.

And they said to him: if you desire to use this Sword the mystical formula of divine names and to hand it down to the generations that follow you, a person who binds himself to use it must sanctify himself for three days from seminal emission and from ritual impurity.

If for secret matters one wishes to take and to bind a man and a woman so they shall be one with each other; or to nullify harmful spirits and signs; or to bind a ship; or to bring a man out of prison; for any such thing write on a red tassa a metal plate or lamella from the section "Tuvir Tasbir" until the section "Ha Bishmahat" [these are reference points within the long list of names in the Sword].

kb.t: The Sword of Moses (Ḥarba de-Moshe)
kb.th: The Sword of Moses is a working manual of name-magic that adjures angelic ministers and sets that adjuration inside the daily prayer.
h: The work's operations rest on adjuring the angelic ministers of the Sword ([p. 87](/book/6a7de037fd8615d37af98df8?page=87)).
The user is told to insert the adjuration into the 'Who hears prayer' blessing of the daily prayer ([p. 87](/book/6a7de037fd8615d37af98df8?page=87)).
It belongs with Hebrew practical texts in which an amulet is labelled 'tested and proven', the empirical formula of the segulot literature (p. 223).
tr: Hebrew practical manuscripts head such recipes 'Segulah', the practitioner's own word for a remedy or efficacious charm, with the cure said to come 'by the help of the Blessed Name' (p. 270).
an: Maimonides objects to name-magic of this type: the invented names of amulet writers have no power, and a perfect man should not even listen to them ([p. 180](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=180)).

q.t: Some wicked women, reverting to Satan, and seduced by the illusions and phantasms of demons, believe and profess that they ride at night with Diana on certain beasts, with an innumerable multitude of women, passing over immense distances
it was adopted by the canonists and embodied in the successive collections of Regino, Burchard, Ivo, and Gratian—the latter giving it the stamp of unquestioned authority
Bishop Burchard, in the eleventh century, when copying the text, came to add to Diana, Herodias,
In some way this utterance came to be attributed to a Council of Anquira, which could never be identified

kb.t: Canon Episcopi
kb.th: The Canon Episcopi holds that women who believe they ride at night with Diana are deceived by demonic illusions, and that believing in the ride is itself a loss of faith.
h: Women who believe they ride at night with Diana on beasts over great distances are deceived by demonic illusions ([p. 511](/book/699069542f82e0fda4806eb6?page=511)).
Whoever believes such things has lost the faith ([p. 511](/book/699069542f82e0fda4806eb6?page=511)).

The canon passed through the collections of Regino, Burchard, Ivo and Gratian; Burchard added Herodias to Diana, and Gratian gave it unquestioned authority ([p. 512](/book/699069542f82e0fda4806eb6?page=512)).
an: Lea shows that its ascription to a Council of Ancyra is spurious, since the council was never identified and the text first appears in a fragment of no later than the ninth century ([p. 512](/book/699069542f82e0fda4806eb6?page=512)).

A treatise of c. 1445 cites the canon to rule that the night ride cannot happen bodily, only in spirit through diabolical illusion, since no such goddess exists ([p. 132](/book/69905e1a2fd6a039938a0f5d?page=132)).

Pseudo-Aristotle, The Secret of Secrets.a: The work lists talismans (talsamāt) among its specialized sciences, together with the secrets of the stars, the use of forces, and the properties of stones and plants. The Tenth Treatise is assigned to these subjects. In the passage on talismans, upper celestial things each have a portion, and the lower world is influenced by the strongest talismans. Their making is observed in a space not interrupted by the connection and light of the planets.

q.t: Know that for every one of the upper [celestial] things, there is a portion of the decrease, and likewise, what remains of the lower [terrestrial] world is influenced by the strongest talsamāt talismans.

On the specialized sciences of Talismans magical objects/occult science, the secrets of the stars, the use of forces, and the properties of stones and plants, from what is beneficial in what I have presented, God willing.
the science of divination and omens and the like, the science of magic, incantations, alchemy, mechanics and the like, the science of crafts and trades

In similar fashion, the masters of tilsamat talismans worked in setting them up after their knowledge of the natures of things, their properties, their similarities, and the method of their composition and the ratios of their assembly.

Some of them believe and hold that the celestial bodies are indications of events in this world before they occur. Others believe and hold that they also possess actions and influences along with their indications.

kb.t: Ikhwān al-Ṣafāʾ, Epistles (Rasāʾil), with the epistle on magic
kb.th: The Brethren of Purity file magic among the sciences of their encyclopaedia and treat talisman-making as a craft comparable to medicine.
h: The science of magic and incantations sits among the propaedeutic sciences, beside divination, alchemy, mechanics and the trades ([p. 166](/book/69b6363a8ab57a1de53a75c8?page=166)).

One epistle is devoted to the essence of magic and incantations, covering the evil eye, omens, spells, talismans, and how jinn, devils and spiritual beings act on one another ([p. 19](/book/69b6363a8ab57a1de53a75c8?page=19)).
Talisman-makers are like physicians compounding remedies, and the nine-cell square for easing childbirth is their example ([p. 121](/book/69b6363a8ab57a1de53a75c8?page=121)).
an: The Picatrix likewise models the composite talisman on compound medicine, as physicians compound simples into electuaries ([p. 54](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=54)).

Kanjur, Tantra section (rGyud 'bum)|||Ti.a: The tantra passages link mantra to a range of rites: subjugation (abhichara), pacification, enrichment, power, the fire hearth homa, torma offerings, and medical treatment for poison. The Wrathful King is spoken to tame harmful beings including nagas, yakshas, kumbhandas and putanas, and the sound Hum closes off obstructors. One passage says the power of secret mantras does not arise from the mantras or from substances but is the blessing of the secret mantra. It also says the practice should not be explained to faithless or cruel beings.

q.t: Also, explain the divisions of activity, and thoroughly explain the rites of subjugation abhichara. Through the rites of pacification, enrichment, and power, how does the Lord make it very swift?
Furthermore, regarding other obstructors and misleading spirits: as the mantra practitioner proclaims the sound Hum, they will find no further opportunity [to cause harm].

It is like this: for example, through secret mantras, poison and fever and so forth are made to be absent. It is like this: the goddesses called Mamos wrathful female spirits send infectious diseases to sentient beings through secret mantras.
In short, Magic is that whose cause is hidden from most minds and whose derivation is difficult to deduce.
In contrast, the subject of a Talisman is "spirit within a body," and the subject of Alchemy is "body within a body."
Know that whoever makes a choice of timing has effectively created a talisman; this is an essential principle.
do not perform any work until the Moon is in the specific degree that corresponds to that work.

kb.t: Picatrix (Ghāyat al-ḥakīm)
kb.th: The Picatrix treats magic as the knowledge of hidden causes and builds a full theory of astral and talismanic work on it, with stars, occult properties, the operator's will and the spoken word as its powers.
h: Images in the lower world are subject to celestial images, and choosing an astrological moment is already the making of a talisman ([p. 37](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=37)); ([p. 14](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=14)).
Talismans are timed by the 28 lunar mansions of the Indian Sages, and no work may begin until the Moon stands in its proper degree ([p. 17](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=17)).

Practical magic works through the specific properties (khawāṣṣ) of minerals, plants and animals, and the talisman is compounded like a physician's medicine ([p. 14](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=14)); ([p. 54](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=54)).
The operator's certainty strengthens the rational soul so that the will connects with the World Soul ([p. 17](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=17)).

Speech is the finest kind of common magic, and the words spoken over a talisman are to it what the soul is to the body ([p. 14](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=14)); ([p. 29](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=29)).
tr: Its word is siḥr, which it defines neutrally as whatever has a cause hidden from most minds and a derivation hard to deduce, a practitioner's use of a word that elsewhere in Arabic leans toward the satanic ([p. 13](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=13)).
It sorts the operative arts by subject: nīranj is spirit within spirit, the talisman is spirit within a body, and alchemy is body within body ([p. 13](/book/695361879c494f9f9f0424f4?page=13)).
an: Thorndike judged the Latin Picatrix a confused compilation and a hodgepodge of recipes, against reading it as a systematic theory of magic ([p. 829](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=829)).

q.t: The nature of demons is not without a body; but it has a body, and moves about concerning bodies, which our venerable fathers have also judged.

They gather on the day on which the Savior suffered, in the evening, in an appointed place together with girls known to them. And after certain sacred rites, with the lights extinguished, they mingle together
And he said, "I am amazed that you are ignorant of this, that in no muscle or nerve does the feeling reside, but in the spirit that exists within them.

kb.t: Michael Psellos (attrib.), On the Operation of Daemons
kb.th: The dialogue on daemons ascribed to Psellos treats daemons as embodied beings of air and defines goeteia as the art that works through the lowest, material daemons to show phantoms to onlookers.
h: Daemons are not bodiless; they have thin, airy bodies, and the work cites Basil that even angels have them ([p. 179](/book/69b4cc25d2bf9b45ea47822e?page=179)).
It reports a teacher who held there are six general kinds of daemons, perhaps because the whole daemonic race is body-loving and six is the bodily, worldly number (p. 134).

It accuses the Euchites of a demon-worshipping rite on Good Friday evening, with the lights put out and incestuous mingling, an accusation pattern later attached to the witches' sabbath ([p. 188](/book/69b4cc25d2bf9b45ea47822e?page=188)).
It calls the material and subterranean daemons harmful ([p. 74](/book/69592b387c072c27f686e08e?page=74)).
tr: Goeteia here names the art concerned with material and subterranean daemons, which shows their phantoms to onlookers and raises some as if from Hades, so it covers only the chthonic, harmful side of what English calls magic ([p. 74](/book/69592b387c072c27f686e08e?page=74)).

q.t: as is the name Seraphim, Cherubim, Michael, Gabriel. For thus, pronounced according to the dialect of the Hebrews, they have a singular and ineffable efficacy in the administration of sacred things; but when changed into Greek names, they are entirely powerless.

As far as I am concerned, I do not approve of the sacred rites of the Chaldeans at all, nor do I assent to their doctrine. With difficulty, however, I have uncovered the obscurity of the oracle for you.

Inspectio inspection is said to occur when the one initiated into the sacred rites sees divine lights. But if he sees nothing, and the one who orders and prepares the rites observes some specter by himself, this is called superinspectio super-inspection from the perspective of the initiate.

kb.t: Michael Psellos, Exegesis of the Chaldaean Oracles
kb.th: Psellos expounds the Chaldaean Oracles and their account of sacred names while disowning both their rites and their doctrine.
h: Psellos says he approves neither the rites nor the doctrine of the Chaldaeans whose oracles he explains ([p. 96](/book/69b51ebdff09e4fe943b3e60?page=96)).

On the oracle against changing barbarous names, he explains that names like Seraphim, Cherubim, Michael and Gabriel have ineffable efficacy in Hebrew and lose it in Greek ([p. 96](/book/69b51ebdff09e4fe943b3e60?page=96)).

k.g: a rite for enchantment or fascination

q.t: an eight-petaled lotus on birch bark. … having written it, one should wear it on the head; one does not need to recite the mantra.

One should perform the worship of all Yaksini nature spirits with a focused mind. One may visualize them as a sister, a mother, a daughter, or a woman, according to one's desire. One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, stationed on the ground for six nights.

Having written the yantra mystical diagram on turmeric-colored bhūrja-patra birch bark with a focused mind, worship it with yellow flowers and incense. Place it between [the] sesame seeds, [and] a paralysis of speech is sure to occur.

kb.t: Kakṣapuṭa (attributed to Nāgārjuna)
kb.th: The Kakṣapuṭa treats a written figure as able to do the work of a spoken mantra.
h: One rite prescribes writing an eight-petalled lotus on birch bark to be worn on the head ([p. 63](/book/69d7e2147b3ae67b6e6ea9c8?page=63)).
Once the figure is worn, one does not need to recite the mantra, so the written object stands in for the spoken formula ([p. 63](/book/69d7e2147b3ae67b6e6ea9c8?page=63)).

k.g: ritual placement of mantras on the body

q.t: Now I will describe in this tantra the characteristics of the six acts, which yield success in practice according to all the tantras. (121) The wise speak of the six acts: peace, subjection, paralysis, causing malice, driving away, and death.

having broken the effigy into seven parts, one should offer [them] into the kindled fire while reciting the five … (141) The first [part] is the right foot, followed by the right hand. The third is declared to be the head
Satisfying, enlivening, and concealing—these are the ten mantra-processes. The extraction of mantra letters from the Matrika the subtle letters of the alphabet is called generation. (114)

kb.t: Lakṣmaṇadeśika, Śāradātilaka Tantra
kb.th: The Śāradātilaka sets out six ritual acts, from healing to killing, as the common ground of all the tantras, and gives its destructive rite the form of a fire offering.
h: It gives six acts, peace, subjection, paralysis, causing malice, driving away and death, as yielding success according to all the tantras ([p. 269](/book/69d7e10be9e5e67989c373f9?page=269)).
It defines śānti as the removal of diseases and decay and vaśya as making all people obedient ([p. 269](/book/69d7e10be9e5e67989c373f9?page=269)).

Its hostile rite to Kālī breaks an effigy of the enemy into seven parts and offers them into the fire limb by limb while five ṛc verses are recited ([p. 258](/book/69d7e10be9e5e67989c373f9?page=258)).
an: A tantra in the Thadrak Kanjur sums up every accomplishment of the tantras as four kinds of action, pacifying, increasing, subjugating and wrathful, with the hostile rite as the fourth of a sanctioned set ([p. 319](/book/69e7aac85f1a22ab19a8d43f?page=319)).

Seven Rites of Fierce Activity (Raudraka.a: The text lists the activities as pacifying, increasing, separation, magnetizing, summoning, expelling, suppressing and killing. Each follows seven steps: worship, torma offering, mantra recitation, the fire offering homa, turning the wheel of activity, one-pointed meditation, and making good any lack or excess. Yamaraja is summoned and bound to his commitment with mantras, visualization and mudra, and the closing prayers ask the wrathful deities to liberate the consciousness of the sinful ones.

q.t: Furthermore, if one analyzes the combination of mantras and ritual substances with doubt, accomplishments siddhi spiritual attainments or magical powers will not be achieved. If double-mindedness arises, or if one wonders about it, or if faith declines, then even if the accomplishment is near, it will undoubtedly be turned back.
By reciting this, visualize that hook-like light rays emanate from your heart center, bringing Yamaraja the King of Death and his retinue to that place.
Now is the time for your compassion! For those sinful ones who cause the teaching to decline, At this time, liberate them from their life-force and evil karma.

Tengyur, tantra commentaries (rGyud 'gre.a: The rites pair mantra counts with visualization. A preliminary retreat runs 300,000 to 700,000 recitations, with torma sprinkled and 'divine pride' held that the mantra is the Goddess's speech. Light rays like poison arrows deliver a 'mustard seed strike' and 'blood strike' into a triangular pit, and an invincible army destroys the target's body and land.

q.t: Strike with the poison arrow of death and kill with madness! Send forth bad omens such as wild beasts and the Garuda a mythical bird-like creature! Perform this work of protecting the teachings quickly!

Contemplate that an invincible army, many filled with the five poisons, many holding mustard seed weapons, and many holding physical weapons, destroy the body and the land of the enemy, killing and eating everyone.
Next, twist three threads together while reciting the "all-purpose" karma mantra. Tie three knots in the thread and bind it to the student’s right hand for the purpose of protection.

Maimonides establishes two kinds of magic here: one is demonic, the other is illusory. … Maimonides says such people are to be stoned. … Such imposters are to be punished with lashes according to Maimonides.

kb.t: Moses Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Idolatry 11
kb.th: Maimonides' code treats magic as a branch of idolatry and separates demonic magic, a capital offence, from sleight of hand, a lesser one.
h: Magical acts are a form of star worship, so every magician is an idolater who must be put to death ([p. 570](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=570)).
The magicians Maimonides read held that no magical work succeeds without regard to the stars, every plant, animal and metal having its own star ([p. 570](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=570)).
A 1668 Latin commentary reads the Laws of Idolatry as distinguishing demonic magic, punished by stoning, from sleight of hand, punished by lashes ([p. 168](/book/69c89ffe6c6f3cc53c85deb7?page=168)).

q.t: But no magical work can be performed without respect and consideration for the Stars. For they think that every Plant has its own Star, just as they also assign certain Stars to all Animals and Metals.

They even think that those works are specific forms of worship of the Stars … therefore it necessarily follows that every Magician must be killed; … because every Magician is without doubt an Idolater
And because the greater part of those works are to be performed by Women, therefore the Law says; A sorceress [Mekhashefah], that is, a female magician or illusionist, you shall not suffer to live.

God said to them in the words of the Covenant that because of the idolatry and magic through which they believe they can ward off these harms, those very same evils will instead remain and dwell upon them.

kb.t: Moses Maimonides, Guide of the Perplexed III.37 and I.61–62
kb.th: Maimonides treats magic as a form of star worship inherited from the Sabians and Chaldaeans, forbidden as idolatry, and dismisses the divine names of amulet writers as powerless inventions.
h: Astrology and magic come from the Sabians, Chaldaeans, Egyptians and Canaanites, and the commandments against them exist to restrain idolatry (Guide III.37); ([p. 569](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=569)).

The magicians he read held that no work succeeds without regard to the stars, each plant, animal and metal having its own star, so magic is star worship and every magician an idolater who must be put to death ([p. 570](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=570)).
The covenant curses, wild beasts and crop damage, threaten as punishment the very harms magicians claim to avert ([p. 571](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=571)).

Divine names heard from amulet writers should be ignored: the writers are superstitious and insane, and the names they invent mean nothing (Guide I.61); ([p. 180](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=180)).

Only the Tetragrammaton is the Shem ha-Mephorash, and the Twelve- and Forty-Two-Letter Names taught concepts, not the sounds of letters ([p. 180](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=180)); ([p. 127](/book/6974b642457dd8909910b9e5?page=127)).
tr: Maimonides explains the feminine 'sorceress' of Exodus 22:18 by saying that most of these magical works are performed by women ([p. 570](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=570)).
an: Galatinus's De arcanis (1518) cites Guide I.61 for saying Adonai in place of the ineffable name outside the priestly blessing ([p. 117](/book/6974b642457dd8909910b9e5?page=117)).

al-Būnī, The Radiant Sparks (al-Lumʿa al.a: Al-Būnī says a response comes quickly when the time, the seeker's spiritual state, the fitting Name and the heart's focus on its goal are joined. He assigns groups of divine Names to kinds of seekers, with stated effects such as humbling a tyrant or ending the pain of hunger. He also says that sustained dhikr brings the ruhaniyyat of the Names near to recite with the practitioner, and he mentions carving a Name on a silver ring set by a wafq.

q.t: When the knowledge of the time, the knowledge of the spiritual state, and the knowledge of the Name appropriate to that time and the need matching that Name and time are all combined—along with the heart’s focus on that specific desired goal—the result is a speedy response.

No lowly person mentions them except that he becomes mighty; no insignificant person mentions them except that he is elevated. If mentioned before a tyrant, that tyrant is humbled; if before one of the kings of the earth, that king will find within himself humility and denial of his own ego.

As for al-Samad, it is an invocation suitable specifically for those practicing self-discipline through hunger [original: "al-murtadin bi-l-ju‘," those training the soul via fasting]. Its ultimate effect is that one will not feel the pain of hunger at all, so long as no other invocation interferes with it.
For numbers have an effect on humans that they do not perceive, for His power is glorified.
Know that the servants of these two noble names are among the believing angels

The spirits have bowed low; four of their servants will come to you, one will be pleasant in his presence and will stand before you. If you greet him with peace, he is a great king. You may dispose of him in whatever you wish after he takes the covenant and pledge from you, and he stipulates a condition upon you: do not lie in your speech, do not eat garlic, and do not commit indecent acts.

kb.t: al-Būnī, The Sun of Knowledge (Shams al-maʿārif)
kb.th: The Shams al-maʿārif teaches that letters and numbers carry a hidden spiritual power, and that the angelic servants of the divine names act for the pious operator.
h: Numbers have a spiritual power that acts on people imperceptibly, which is why the letters hold secrets of benefit ([p. 10](/book/69908a7693003de39c9658e5?page=10)).

The angelic servants of two divine names will leave a gold dinar under the pillow each night for one who keeps conditions of piety, grave-visiting and recitation ([p. 103](/book/69908a7693003de39c9658e5?page=103)).
an: Agrippa in the Latin West likewise holds that numbers, as the most formal of mathematical things, have greater and more hidden virtues than natural things ([p. 220](/book/698420e1f1fb376a3d58061c?page=220)).

k.g: a system of magical prayers and figures intended to grant knowledge and memory
symbolic sigils or marks used in the Notory Art

q.t: which the Moſt High Creator by his holy Angel miniſtred to S O L O M O N upon the Altar of the Temple; that thereby in a ſhort time he knew all Arts and Sciences, both Liberal and Mechanick,

Hydromancy is a science of divining by the Water; whereby the Masters thereof judged by the standing or running of the Water. Pyromancy is an Experiment of divining by the flaming of the fire; which the antient Philosophers esteemed of great efficacy.

Grant the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit so that I may be able to scrutinize, rightly, quickly, and perfectly understand, retain in memory, worthily reveal, and lovingly proclaim the wonderful and venerable mysteries of your secrets with pious trembling, reverence, and due devotion of heart.

kb.t: Ars notoria (The Notory Art of Solomon)
kb.th: The Ars notoria presents itself as a revealed art of prayers and figures by which all knowledge may be gained quickly, as it was by Solomon.
h: An angel revealed the art to Solomon on the Temple altar ([p. 9](/book/69592ee9a41e40e9146a4289?page=9)).
By this art Solomon came to know all the liberal and mechanical arts in a short time ([p. 9](/book/69592ee9a41e40e9146a4289?page=9)).
an: Waite named back-dating and imputed authorship as the two crying bibliographical sins of grimoires, which tells against taking the book's Solomonic attribution at face value ([p. 49](/book/69c896426c6f3cc53c85c4ea?page=49)).

k.g: the practice of astrological and celestial manipulation

q.t: Generally calling it "magic," we understand it for all things hidden from the sense, and which the greater part do not apprehend, how they are made or by what causes they happen.
For He alone is the first, the perfect philosophy, and the science of truth. … true science is goodness that proceeds from Him
its works are from Spirit to Spirit … the composition of images is spirit in body

how one can speak with the spirits of the planets … in the fourth, indeed, [it treats] of the properties of the spirits and of those things which are necessary and to be observed in this art, and how it is aided by images

kb.t: Picatrix (Latin)
kb.th: The Picatrix treats magic as a science grounded in God, covering everything hidden from the senses whose causes most people do not grasp, and works it chiefly by putting spirit into bodies through images.
h: Magic is everything hidden from the senses whose manner and causes most people do not grasp ([p. 16](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=16)).
True science proceeds from God, whom the book calls the perfect philosophy and the science of truth ([p. 14](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=14)).
Its science works from spirit to spirit, and making an image or talisman means putting spirit into body ([p. 16](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=16)).

Its four books run from celestial images and the figures of the heavens to planetary properties, speaking with planetary spirits, and the powers of spirits aided by images and suffumigations ([p. 12](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=12)); ([p. 201](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=201)).
Its procedures call for vile and obscene ingredients, such as a magic mirror suffumigated with seven products of the human body ([p. 831](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=831)).
tr: The book uses 'magic' in a broad, neutral sense for any working whose causes are hidden, and reserves 'nigromantia' for the part that speaks with planetary spirits ([p. 16](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=16)); ([p. 12](/book/69d665f8bf5afe33937f8a3f?page=12)).
an: Thorndike judged that the Picatrix treats magic as a science and a superior branch of learning, with astronomical images and invocations of demons as its two leading features ([p. 830](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=830)).
The Speculum astronomiae is said to list 'Picatrices' among the image books, alongside Zael and the books of Hermes on images ([p. 50](/book/69906ed28a353648e1ed04da?page=50)).

q.t: he brought the book of secrets to Adam, who was sad and grieving because he saw that he was separated and far removed from wisdom. And this book was written upon a sapphire stone.
through this book, containing the holy and glorious names of God which are within it, Adam knew those things he wished to know and did those things he wished to do.
Image is called the Word of God, according to Raziel. … Upon that image must be the names of the angels written above the chapters
Fear the Creator of all that is made and look into this book, which is called the Book of Virtues and Miracles, regarding holiness and purity.

kb.t: Book of Raziel (Liber Razielis), Latin
kb.th: The Liber Razielis presents itself as a book of secrets given to Adam, whose power to know and to act lies in the holy names of God it contains, to be used in holiness and purity.
h: The angel Raziel brought Adam, grieving over his lost wisdom, a book of secrets written on a sapphire stone ([p. 6](/book/699067e68da6face82f779a6?page=6)).
Through the holy names of God in the book, Adam knew and did what he wished, and later prophets worked with it ([p. 6](/book/699067e68da6face82f779a6?page=6)).
Incenses belong to the four quarters and elements, and knowing how to compound them is a precondition for working with the book ([p. 93](/book/699067e68da6face82f779a6?page=93)).
The 'image' used in its operations is the Word of God, and angel names must be written on it ([p. 309](/book/699067e68da6face82f779a6?page=309)).
It calls itself a Book of Virtues and Miracles, to be used in fear of the Creator, in holiness and purity, after fumigating and burying the image ([p. 309](/book/699067e68da6face82f779a6?page=309)).
an: Maimonides objected that the invented names of amulet writers have no power and that a perfect man should not even listen to them, an objection aimed at name-based works of the Raziel type ([p. 180](/book/697a8670e680cef7cedae3aa?page=180)).

Montgomery traced angel names on the Nippur incantation bowls to the Book of Raziel, linking late-antique Babylonian Jewish magic with the later Raziel literature ([p. 159](/book/6953af0577f38f6761bd92a5?page=159)).

q.t: for although this part is a part of necromancy according to that species of necromancy which is subalternated to astronomy, and which is called that of images and seals … nor can it be known unless astronomy, magic, and the sciences of necromancy are known simultaneously.

One must know the cause of this from the science of the magicians which the Greek Magor, the Babylonian Germa, and the Egyptian Hermes completed in the beginning … the figures of the heavens are the first figures

the Greek Magor, the Babylonian Germa, and the Egyptian Hermes

kb.t: Albertus Magnus, On Minerals (De mineralibus) II.3, on images in stones
kb.th: Albertus treats engraved images and seals in stones as a real art that draws its force from the heavens, while filing it under necromancy and warning against natural look-alikes and fakes.
h: The principle of the art, taken from 'the science of the magicians' such as Germa and Hermes, is that the figures of the heavens are the first figures and act on every figure made by nature or art ([p. 59](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=59)).

Gems and metal images must be cut at observed times when the celestial force is strongest, and fiery signs such as Aries, Leo or Sagittarius cut in a stone give it a property against fevers, dropsy and paralysis ([p. 60](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=60)); ([p. 61](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=61)).
An image's celestial virtue lasts only for a period, after which 'the cold and dead image' is useless, which is why ancient images no longer work ([p. 60](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=60)).

Some figures in stone are painted by nature, as a king's head Albertus saw in a sawn marble at Venice, and some are frauds hardened by alchemists with lac virginis ([p. 56](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=56)); ([p. 58](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=58)).
Stones have no soul; their wondrous virtues follow from the stone as a whole compound ([p. 32](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=32)).
tr: Albertus calls the doctrine of images and seals a part of necromancy subordinate to astronomy, which cannot be known without astronomy, magic and necromancy together, and he treats it anyway at his associates' request ([p. 56](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=56)).
an: Read beside the Speculum astronomiae, this work names that book's abominable authors as founders and teaches their art, so the Speculum's clean split between licit and illicit images is not Albertus's only line ([p. 56](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=56)).

k.g: Ars Notoria, a medieval grimoire for gaining knowledge through rituals

q.t: Now all that which exists without the operation of nature or of art is not a natural thing at all; that is to say, it is a feigned thing, surrounded by frauds and

In these, a wise man ought to possess this prudence: to neglect the incantations and characters, and to test the work of nature and art. And thus he will see both animate and inanimate things come together because of the conformity of nature, not because of the power of an incantation or a character.
And herein lies the error: that he believes spirits are subject to him and that spirits are compelled by human virtue; for this is impossible, because human power is far inferior to that of spirits.

kb.t: Roger Bacon, Letter on the Secret Works of Art and Nature and the Nullity of Magic
kb.th: Bacon argues that art and nature can do more than any magic, and that wonders made without them are frauds, so magic as commonly claimed is empty.
h: Whatever happens without the work of nature or art is a feigned thing, made by tricks of movement, voice, instruments and darkness ([p. 5](/book/6970e3559b09d309d780a244?page=5)).
The charms and written characters of Bacon's day are false and doubtful, and seemingly occult effects such as the magnet's pull are natural ([p. 9](/book/6970e3559b09d309d780a244?page=9)).

Evil spirits invoked with sacrifices help only as far as God permits for men's sins, and it is far easier to obtain what is useful from God or good spirits ([p. 8](/book/6970e3559b09d309d780a244?page=8)).
Art can make ships that move without rowers and chariots that move without animals, so all magical power falls below the works of art and nature ([p. 24](/book/69c866086c6f3cc53c856325?page=24)).
an: Webster (1677) invokes the letter, with Dee's notes, to argue that witch belief comes from ignorance of the power of art and nature and that it is unworthy to credit devils with what these produce ([p. 287](/book/69906181322e01b1349a4aa9?page=287)).

k.g: divine worship due to God alone

From which it is clearly apparent that these men, and others like them, were of the opinion that the vices which appear in their judgments [referring to astrological or divinatory judgments] are brought about by the admission or influence of evil spirits, just as the arioli soothsayers/diviners and magi sorcerers do.

I return to the general history, and by many [authors] it is shown that almost all of antiquity that was occupied with these things had bad ends, because the art of magia magic is the author and the apologist of evil.

kb.t: Speculum astronomiae
kb.th: The Speculum astronomiae defends astrology and draws a line among images: those worked by fumigation, invocation or named spirits are rejected, while images that act by the heavens alone are accepted as the highest part of astronomy.
h: It sorts images into three kinds: the abominable, the detestable ones with characters and names such as the rings of Solomon, and purely astronomical images, which it calls the sublimest part of astronomy ([p. 712](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=712)).
The abominable kind works with fumigations and invocations; a margin calls it the worst idolatry and the text rejects it ([p. 46](/book/69906ed28a353648e1ed04da?page=46)).

The detestable kind exorcises spirits by name, citing the Almandal of Solomon and a book called Rasiel, and is suspect because names in an unknown tongue may hide something against the Catholic faith ([p. 47](/book/69906ed28a353648e1ed04da?page=47)); ([p. 713](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=713)).
Astronomical images use no fumigations, invocations or inscribed characters and work by their own nature as constrained by the heavens ([p. 50](/book/69906ed28a353648e1ed04da?page=50)).
Its bibliography of image books is said to name Zael's book of images, books of Hermes on images, and 'Picatrices' ([p. 50](/book/69906ed28a353648e1ed04da?page=50)).
an: Thorndike defended Albertus Magnus as author against Mandonnet's attribution to Roger Bacon, which he said rested on very little evidence ([p. 707](/book/699069252f82e0fda48046c3?page=707)).

Albertus's undisputed De mineralibus files images and seals under necromancy and names Germa and Hermes, the Speculum's abominable authors, as founders, so the Speculum's clean line is not the only Albertine one ([p. 56](/book/69af21d4f98f6eff774cb8bf?page=56)).

q.t: Whence they cannot formally transmute lower bodies unless by applying some bodily and continuous things proportioned to the effects.

This appears manifestly false, because there is found some operation of demons that in no way can proceed from other natural causes. For example, someone seized by a demon speaks an unknown language, and many other works of demons are found, both in the possessed and in the arts of necromancy, which in no way can come from any intellect except those to which others are constrained.

kb.t: Thomas Aquinas, On Evil (De malo) q. 16, on demons
kb.th: Aquinas limits what demons can do to bodies: they cannot change the form of matter by their own power, though they can work on the senses and the imagination.
h: Demons cannot formally transmute lower bodies except by applying bodily agents suited to the effect, as a man heats something with fire ([p. 339](/book/69dbcc290f8c5edf20f46beb?page=339)).
Demons cannot imprint bodily forms on matter, yet they can alter a person's senses and imagination ([p. 343](/book/69dbcc290f8c5edf20f46beb?page=343)).

Zakariyyāʾ al-Qazwīnī, Wonders of Creati.a: Al-Qazwīnī describes ʿarrafah as deducing one event from another through a hidden connection, and says the souls of diviners know events through signs. He gives examples of the Banu Mudlij reading lineage and of diviners consulted by Alexander and by Persian kings.

q.t: ‘Arrafah is the act of deducing one event from another based on a hidden connection between them. It is said that Alexander the Great went to the Sikl likely a region or city and saw a female diviner there.
If one is so afflicted, they write charms against him, for the demon will pursue the madman until he destroys him.

The first is that magical science is not bad, for by its knowledge, evil can be avoided and good pursued.
